description: Siamo Efesto, un team di ingegneri aerospaziali dedicato alla sicurezza delle missioni umane su Luna e Marte. Sviluppiamo una dashboard basata su intelligenza artificiale per analizzare i dati NASA PSI sulla combustione in microgravità.
summary: NAVI (Neural Analysis of Variable-Gravity Ignition) — Flame in Freefall is an end-to-end engineering AI co-pilot designed to ensure fire safety in lunar and extraterrestrial habitats for the Artemis generation. In lunar gravity (0.165*g) and hypobaric, oxygen-enriched atmospheres (56.5 kPa, 34% O_2), fire behaves unpredictably, turning flame-retardant materials flammable while delaying smoke detection. Meanwhile, decades of NASA data remain trapped in fragmented spreadsheets and PDFs, forcing aerospace contractors to spend weeks and millions on parabolic flights and drop towers. NAVI solves this by combining a zero-hallucination AI assistant—querying nearly 16,000 normalized NASA PSI data points via deterministic SQL and 300+ report pages with exact DOI citations—with one-click NASA-STD-3001 compliance auditing, a real-time 2D Artemis habitat fire simulator, and a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) that leverages the P^(1.8)*g scaling law to replicate lunar fires in affordable ground chambers.
details:
NAVI (Neural Analysis of Variable-Gravity Ignition) — Flame in Freefall is an end-to-end engineering AI co-pilot and simulation platform built to ensure fire safety in lunar and extraterrestrial habitats for the Artemis generation.

NAVI unifies fragmented NASA Physical Science Informatics (PSI) research with predictive physics and automated regulatory auditing across four modules:

  • Zero-Hallucination AI Co-Pilot: Queries nearly 16,000 normalized NASA experimental data points via read-only DuckDB SQL and searches 300+ report pages via hybrid RAG (ChromaDB + BM25), returning instant Plotly charts and exact DOI citations.
  • Automated Safety Compliance: Audits internal simulations and uploaded CSV/Excel files against NASA-STD-3001, OCHMO-TB-008, and SMAC limits in one click.
  • 2D Artemis MPH Simulator: Models real-time flame spread, heat release, and CO buildup using flight materials (SIBAL, Nomex, Kapton, ETFE) at lunar gravity (0.165 g) and Artemis cabin conditions (56.5 kPa, 34% O2).
  • Multi-Gravity PINN Lab: Combines six NASA campaigns with a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) trained on BASS-II data to compare Earth, Moon, and microgravity regimes.

In lunar gravity and oxygen-enriched habitats, flame standoff increases up to 110%, smoke detection slows down, and flame-retardant materials become flammable. NAVI compresses safety validation from weeks to seconds and slashes testing costs by applying the P^1.8 * g scaling law to calculate the reduced Earth-chamber pressure needed to replicate lunar flames—cutting reliance on expensive parabolic flights and drop towers. It empowers researchers globally while giving Artemis contractors and space insurers an objective pre-launch risk standard.


Built in Python using Streamlit, Plotly, Pandas, Parquet, and in-memory DuckDB. The AI layer uses the Anthropic Claude SDK with tool calling and quantized ONNX all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings (avoiding heavy PyTorch dependencies), paired with vectorized NumPy/SciPy solvers and a PINN model. It runs efficiently on standard CPUs without GPUs.

Rather than a generic chatbot, NAVI bridges deterministic SQL analytics, physics-informed machine learning, and regulatory compliance. Key design factors included eliminating numerical hallucinations, ensuring 100% offline/air-gapped operation to meet aerospace ITAR privacy requirements, referencing strict SMAC toxicity standards, and keeping compute lightweight for affordable cloud scaling.
